annotation.interpretation_a: The 'previously received' refers to the most recent MAX_PUSH_ID frame. Any subsequent frame with a lower value triggers an error.
annotation.interpretation_b: The 'previously received' refers to the initial MAX_PUSH_ID value established at the start of the connection. Any frame with a lower value than the initial value triggers an error.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'previously received' is open to interpretation. Does it mean the last MAX_PUSH_ID frame sent, or the very first one? This impacts implementation because a server might legitimately want to reduce the maximum Push ID after initial negotiation, but the clause, as written, could incorrectly treat that as an error.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether 'previously received' refers to the most recent MAX_PUSH_ID frame or the initial value. This affects how the constraint is applied and whether a server can dynamically reduce the maximum Push ID over time.
